body:
Approved implementation plan (auto-approved gate, epic #99 autonomous run)

Design: separate tables per tier (global_user_site_rules, global_site_blocklist_rules; global_site_rules dropped by migration 002). Precedence: per-agent named > per-agent * > global user > signed blocklist > default allow; tiers before specificity. Global toggle renamed to config key global_tier_enabled and gates the whole global tier; route renamed to POST /api/ui/sites/global-tier/toggle. Updater always writes the signed tier. Migration 002 prefixes the blocklist meta version with pre-002: so the next fetch restores signed rows that user rules previously masked. isAllowed contract frozen: {allowed, decision, source: agent_override|global_user|global_site_blocklist|default, domain, matchedDomain ('*' on wildcard match)}.

Sub-tasks:
- [sub-task 1] Schema + migration 002 + db test updates + new migration-002 tests (complex)
- [sub-task 2] Rewrite site-policy tests first incl. four worked examples (standard)
- [sub-task 3] Engine + CRUD rewrite in site-policy.js (complex) — after 1, 2
- [sub-task 4] Updater: always write signed tier, count signed table, new tests (standard) — after 3
- [sub-task 5] server.js routes: listGlobalRules, wildcard rejection, toggle route rename, popup globalTierEnabled field (standard) — after 3, 4
- [sub-task 6] Web UI client rename to toggleGlobalTier (light) — parallel with 5
- [sub-task 7] CHANGELOG entry (light)
- [sub-task 8] Final verification: full test suite + stale-identifier grep (light) — last

Decisions: keep toggle value on upgrade and warn at migration; defer agent-tier identifier rename to #104; popup client untouched until #105.

Implementation status (auto-approved gate, epic #99 autonomous run)
